 Zoom for Windows: Attackers can escalate privileges over the network
 Zoom has fixed two serious Windows security flaws that enable privilege escalation with updated software packages.

 By
 Dirk Knop 
 Advertisement
 The Zoom web conferencing software has two vulnerabilities that allow attackers on the network to escalate their privileges. They can do so without logging in first, but according to the CVSS rating, the attack requires victim interaction. Updated software is available to fix the flaws in the Windows version.
 Continue after ad
 Zoom describes the vulnerabilities only briefly and superficially. Due to insufficient input validation in Zoom Workplace for Windows , unauthenticated attackers can trigger a privilege escalation over the network. Zoom doesn’t explain what an attack might look like or how to recognize one (CVE-2026-108186, CVSS 9.6 , risk “ critical ”). A faulty origin check can also allow unauthenticated malicious actors on the network to escalate their privileges (CVE-2026-108187, CVSS 8.1 , risk “ high ”).
 Patched software versions
 Zoom Workplace for Windows is vulnerable to the critical security flaw starting with version 7.1.0; the second vulnerability also appears to affect older versions. Version 7.1.8 fixes the more serious flaw, while Zoom Workplace for Windows 7.1.5 fixes the high-risk one. Version 7.2.5 is currently available for download from Zoom’s website and fixes the security issues and presumably others. On Windows, WinGet can also help bring Zoom apps up to date. Running winget upgrade --all at the command prompt provides updates for various installed programs.
 Zoom’s Offensive Security team found the critical flaw internally; a security researcher using the pseudonym shmoul reported the second. The two vulnerabilities apparently aren’t being exploited online yet — at least, Zoom doesn’t say they are.
